I think it needs more clarification on how it does conversions. Stock values, prices of goods and commodities, as well as exchange rates between currencies are all fairly complex things, with a lot of variation. They are not consistent, unless under specific contexts.

Conversion rates, as an example, change depending on the trader, the costs added to the transaction, the volume of the transaction, and the other people around wanting to exchange.

item.content:encoded:
I liked this! It could be a rather dull article in the wrong hands, but you executed it well. And this line made me laugh:

The off-site researcher was contacted by police after this test due to suspicious use of the subject's account.

However, I do have one question. In the experiment with the lottery ticket, there's no mention of how the researcher gets their ticket back from the test subject. If the SCP can make someone jump into a superheated room for a $0.01 payout, I can't imagine it would let someone willingly relinquish a $15 lotto ticket. I suppose that after returning the SCP to the 'bank', the subject may have been more willing to return the ticket, but from the text it isn't clear, and made me wonder exactly what happened.

That aside, what Yoric has said. Upvoted!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Hmm
Containment procedures i don't like.
Firstly, resetting that long a combination every half-hour is stupid - it'd take bloody long to crack, and since it makes it a problem to memorise, it creates a weak spot from where they get the numbers. Everyone of level-3 clearance having the code memorised, and it changing when clearance changes seems saner.

Also - apprehending those with half dollars makes sense only if it goes missing - i imagine there are snack machines in Foundation buildings and it'd be incredibly impractical to check all currency around. Never mind a thief sure as hell wouldn't be seen "handling" the item.

As for the item - Scrooge McDuck's coin? Not too impressed, but not bad enough to downvote, that is, if you make up a saner containment procedure
